Name: FarmChronicle Developer Resource - Calendar and Scheduling Architecture for SMAPI
Author: jwcalendar
Description:
[size=4][b]FarmChronicle Developer Resource[/b][/size]

FarmChronicle is a developer-focused reference project exploring how calendar, planning, scheduling and forecasting systems can be structured for Stardew Valley mods built around SMAPI. This package is intended for mod developers and technically curious users studying date arithmetic, event aggregation, recurring tasks, crop deadline logic, export formats and related architecture.

[size=3][b]Important[/b][/size]
This is a developer resource and architecture reference. It is NOT currently distributed as an installable gameplay mod. The included source has not been compiled or verified inside a local Stardew Valley + SMAPI runtime in the environment where this package was prepared. No DLL is included.

[size=3][b]What's Included[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Calendar/date architecture and Stardew season/year arithmetic[/*]
[*]Crop deadline algorithm design[/*]
[*]Event-provider architecture and recurring-task design[/*]
[*]iCalendar/ICS export architecture[/*]
[*]Multiplayer synchronization design notes[/*]
[*]Caching, performance, testing strategy, SMAPI integration, security and privacy guidance[/*]
[*]C# implementation examples and existing test source files[/*]
[/list][size=3][b]Download File[/b][/size]
Source architecture, technical documentation, examples and test sources for the FarmChronicle developer reference project. This package is not an installable gameplay mod and contains no compiled DLL.

[size=3][b]Topics Covered[/b][/size]
[b]Stardew date arithmetic:[/b] normalized absolute-day representation for four 28-day seasons, comparisons and deterministic sorting, seasonal transitions, and Winter 28 rolling into Spring 1 of the next year.

[b]Crop deadline logic:[/b] supplied-profile calculations based on growth stages, regrowth, season boundaries and multi-season crops. The resource explains assumptions and the missing live game-data adapter; it does not claim verified in-game forecasts.

[b]Event provider architecture:[/b] independent provider concepts for birthdays, festivals, tasks, crops, quests and machine forecasts. The source currently connects only player reminders; other providers are design examples, not active integrations.

[b]iCalendar export:[/b] escaping, deterministic UIDs, UTF-8 line folding, date conversion, event de-duplication and offline export design, with interoperability work still documented.

[b]Multiplayer design:[/b] versioned messages, shared planning state, host authority, malformed-message rejection, and personal versus shared tasks. The source contains a validated message model only; multiplayer transport and synchronization are not implemented.

[size=3][b]Intended Audience[/b][/size]
Useful when building a SMAPI utility, experimenting with date-based game systems, designing task or timeline interfaces, implementing recurring events, studying calendar export, or separating game integration from testable domain logic.
